content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). Steps: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: target sulfonamide -> precursor amine (aryl amine) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). In our target, sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (para to methyl). So we can disconnect to give aniline (the phenyl with methyl) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the other phenyl with the unsaturated amide side chain). So step 1 (retro) is sulfonamide cleavage.

Next, the unsaturated amide side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... This is formed via amide coupling of a carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) with an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retro step: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid and aniline (aniline is c3ccccc3N). The α,β-unsaturated acid is derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So retro step: break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde (probably p-substituted phenyl) and malonic acid (or its derivative). The aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring that also bears the sulfonyl chloride? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The side chain is attached at para position of that phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with an aldehyde at that position (para). So we need aromatic aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (maybe with methyl? Actually the phenyl ring currently has no other substituents besides the sulfonyl group and the side chain. So aldehyde would be c2ccc(CHO)cc2.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

1) Sulfonamide disconnection: target -> sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (methyl phenyl amine). The sulfonyl chloride is the phenyl-sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride). The aniline is the first phenyl ring with methyl (p-toluidine). So product: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl-α,β-unsaturated acid? Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring: ClSO2-Ph-? Wait sulfonyl chloride is Ar-SO2-Cl. So we need Ar = phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid side chain at para position. So precursor: 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl-α,β-unsaturated acid? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring, not to the side chain. So we have Ar-SO2-Cl where Ar is phenyl with para side chain (the unsaturated acid). So we need that acid after step 2.

2) Amide disconnection: the unsaturated acid (Ar-CH=CH-COOH) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we get the unsaturated acid and aniline.

3) Doebner modification: unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde (Ar-CHO) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So we need aromatic aldehyde (same phenyl ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine, aromatic aldehyde (4-formyl phenyl with side chain? Actually the side chain is the same phenyl ring; the aldehyde is on that phenyl). So we need 4-formyl phenyl (para aldehyde) which after Doebner gives unsaturated acid attached to that phenyl. And malonic acid. Also aniline (c3ccccc3N) is separate.

Thus we have three reactions: (1) sulfonamide formation, (2) amide coupling, (3) Doebner modification.

Now we need to find appropriate templates IDs for each step. Use search to find sulfonamide formation template that matches our target. We already searched for sulfonamide formation with product NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1. That gave template ID 733 (template_hash...). That template seems to convert aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline to sulfonamide. So we can use that.

Now amide coupling: need template that forms amide from carboxylic acid and amine. Search for amide formation broken amide. We attempted earlier but got none. Let's search for functional_groups_broken ["amide"] and maybe formed ["carboxylic acid"]? Actually forward reaction: amide formation breaks carboxylic acid (and amine). So broken functional groups: "carboxylic acid". Let's search with broken "carboxylic acid" and formed "amide".
